neighbours.label: the word-piece ' perpet' (perpetuate, perpetually) and the similar piece ' appet' (appetising)
fire: Critics argue that such policies only perpetuate the cycle of poverty.
The two families seemed perpetually at war over the boundary fence.
Old stereotypes are perpetuated by lazy television writing.
The bakery window was full of appetising pastries this morning.
Some legends claim the monks kept a lamp burning perpetually.
The menu offered several appetizing options for vegetarians.
Silence from the board only served to perpetuate the rumours.
Her uncle was perpetually late to every family dinner.
